_warning: These notes are synthetic and contain no real patient data. The expected
codes were assigned from standard ICD-10-CM/CPT/HCPCS references, NOT
reviewed by a certified coder. Treat the resulting numbers as a regression
baseline for prompt and model changes, not as a publishable accuracy claim.
In the 12-case version, three of the expected sets were wrong and the
benchmark blamed the model for them -- assume some of these are wrong too
until a working coder has reviewed every expected set below.
_conventions: Where a code requires specificity (laterality, episode of care, severity,
encounter), the note states it explicitly. Otherwise the benchmark measures
disagreement about documentation-interpretation rules rather than extraction.
E/M codes appear only where total time is stated, using the 2021+ thresholds
Most cases mention orally prescribed drugs and expect NO HCPCS code: billing
a J-code for an outpatient prescription is a known failure mode, and these
cases are the negative controls for it.

cases.note: Established patient here for routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications. A1c 6.9%, stable on metformin. No retinopathy, neuropathy, or nephropathy documented. Total time 25 minutes.

Established patient, 58F, office visit 25 minutes total time for follow-up of type 2 diabetes without complications. A1c reviewed at 8.2%, metformin dose increased. Also reports burning in both feet at night for the past three months; monofilament testing not performed today.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia. Fasting glucose 268 mg/dL today, patient reports missing several doses of metformin. Assessment: type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia. Medication adherence counseling provided.

Follow-up for type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease. eGFR 48, stable. Assessment: type 2 diabetes with diabetic chronic kidney disease, stage 3a. Lisinopril continued for renal protection.
Young adult with type 1 diabetes mellitus without complications, on insulin pump therapy. A1c 7.1%. No evidence of retinopathy, neuropathy, or nephropathy. Pump settings reviewed.
Established patient presents for routine follow-up of essential hypertension. Blood pressure 142/88 today. Lisinopril 10mg continued. No chest pain, no shortness of breath. Total time 15 minutes.
Follow-up for hyperlipidemia. Fasting lipid panel reviewed: LDL 165, HDL 38, triglycerides 190. Atorvastatin started. Diet and exercise counseling provided.
Assessment: pure hypercholesterolemia. LDL 192 with normal triglycerides at 110. Rosuvastatin initiated. Repeat lipid panel in 12 weeks.

Known COPD patient presents with three days of increased dyspnea, increased sputum volume and purulence. Wheezing throughout. Oxygen saturation 91% on room air. Assessment: acute exacerbation of COPD. Prednisone burst and azithromycin prescribed.

Routine follow-up of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. No exacerbation since last visit. Stable on tiotropium. Oxygen saturation 95% on room air, lungs with mildly diminished breath sounds bilaterally.

Established patient with a history of mild intermittent asthma, here for routine review. No exacerbation since last visit, using albuterol less than twice weekly. Lungs clear to auscultation. Continue current regimen.
Assessment: moderate persistent asthma, uncomplicated. Daily symptoms controlled on medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid. No exacerbation currently. Spacer technique reviewed.

Patient presents with wheezing and shortness of breath worsening over two days. Peak flow reduced from baseline. Assessment: asthma with acute exacerbation. Nebulized albuterol given in office with improvement, oral prednisone prescribed.
Follow-up chronic kidney disease. eGFR 22, stable over three months. Assessment: chronic kidney disease, stage 4. Nephrology co-management continued, phosphate binder reviewed.
Follow-up for chronic systolic congestive heart failure. Ejection fraction 32% on recent echocardiogram. Euvolemic today, no orthopnea. Carvedilol and furosemide continued.
Established patient with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. Currently in sinus rhythm on exam and EKG. Apixaban continued, no bleeding. Rate control stable on metoprolol.
Follow-up for hypothyroidism. TSH 3.1 on current levothyroxine dose, within target. No fatigue, cold intolerance, or weight change. Continue same dose.
Assessment: gastroesophageal reflux disease without esophagitis. Symptoms well controlled on omeprazole. No dysphagia, no weight loss, no melena.
Follow-up for obstructive sleep apnea. Compliant with CPAP, averaging 6.5 hours nightly. Daytime somnolence resolved. No mask leak issues reported.
Assessment: benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms. Nocturia three times nightly, weak stream. Tamsulosin started. PSA within normal limits.
Assessment: unilateral primary osteoarthritis of the right knee. Radiographs show medial joint space narrowing. Pain with weight bearing. Physical therapy referral and acetaminophen recommended.
Assessment: iron deficiency anemia. Hemoglobin 10.2, ferritin 8, MCV 74. Oral ferrous sulfate started. Colonoscopy referral placed to evaluate source.
Assessment: morbid obesity due to excess calories. BMI calculated at 42.3 today. Nutrition referral placed, bariatric surgery options discussed.
Patient presents with sore throat and fever, 101.2F. Tonsillar exudate noted on exam. Rapid strep antigen test positive. Amoxicillin prescribed.
Sore throat for two days with rhinorrhea and cough. No tonsillar exudate. Rapid strep antigen test negative. Assessment: acute pharyngitis, viral. Supportive care advised.
Ten days of facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and maxillary tenderness. Assessment: acute maxillary sinusitis. Amoxicillin-clavulanate prescribed.

Child with right ear pain and fever. Right tympanic membrane erythematous and bulging, no perforation. Assessment: acute suppurative otitis media of the right ear without spontaneous rupture. Amoxicillin prescribed.

Left ear pain after swimming. Canal erythematous and edematous with debris, tragal tenderness present. Tympanic membrane intact. Assessment: acute swimmer's ear, left ear. Ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone otic drops prescribed.

Adult female with two days of dysuria and urinary frequency. Urinalysis shows positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites. No flank pain, no fever. Assessment: uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Nitrofurantoin prescribed.

Assessment: acute cystitis without hematuria. Suprapubic discomfort and urgency for three days. Urine culture sent. No fever, no costovertebral angle tenderness. Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prescribed.
Assessment: cellulitis of the right lower limb. Warm, erythematous, tender area over the right shin with demarcated borders. No abscess or fluctuance. No fever. Cephalexin prescribed.
Right eye redness and watery discharge for two days. No pain, no vision change, no photophobia. Assessment: acute conjunctivitis, right eye. Supportive care and hygiene advised.
Abrupt onset fever, myalgia, headache, and dry cough. Rapid influenza test positive. Assessment: influenza with other respiratory manifestations. Oseltamivir prescribed.
Fever, cough, and loss of taste for three days. SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive. Assessment: COVID-19. Isolation instructions given, supportive care advised.

Productive cough, fever, and pleuritic chest pain. Chest x-ray shows right lower lobe infiltrate. Assessment: community-acquired pneumonia, organism unspecified. Amoxicillin prescribed, outpatient management.

Productive cough for eight days with low-grade fever. Chest auscultation reveals scattered rhonchi, no focal consolidation. Chest x-ray not indicated. Assessment: acute bronchitis. Supportive care advised.
Three days of watery diarrhea and vomiting, now improving. No blood in stool, no recent travel or antibiotics. Assessment: viral gastroenteritis. Oral rehydration advised.
Child with honey-crusted lesions around the nares. No systemic symptoms. Assessment: impetigo. Topical mupirocin prescribed.
Itching and scaling between the toes bilaterally with maceration. Assessment: tinea pedis. Topical terbinafine prescribed.
Painful vesicular rash in a single dermatomal distribution on the left trunk, not crossing midline. No ocular involvement. Assessment: herpes zoster without complications. Valacyclovir prescribed.
Hoarseness and voice loss for four days following an upper respiratory infection. No stridor, no dysphagia. Assessment: acute laryngitis. Voice rest and hydration advised.
Sneezing, nasal itching, and clear rhinorrhea every spring. Assessment: allergic rhinitis due to pollen. Intranasal fluticasone prescribed.

Patient inverted the right ankle stepping off a curb yesterday. Swelling and tenderness over the lateral malleolus. Able to bear weight. Ottawa rules negative, no imaging obtained. Assessment: acute sprain of right ankle, initial encounter. A prefabricated off-the-shelf ankle gauntlet orthosis was dispensed in the office today.

Twisted the left ankle playing basketball this morning. Lateral swelling and tenderness, able to bear weight. Assessment: sprain of the left ankle, initial encounter. RICE advised, no durable medical equipment dispensed.

Fall on outstretched right hand today. Wrist deformity and tenderness. Radiographs confirm a closed fracture of the lower end of the right radius. Assessment: fracture of lower end of right radius, initial encounter for closed fracture. Sugar-tong splint applied.

Patient sustained a 2.5 cm linear laceration to the right forearm on a metal edge earlier today. Wound clean, no foreign body, no tendon or nerve involvement. Simple one-layer closure performed with 5-0 nylon. Tetanus up to date.

Patient struck the scalp on a cabinet door, sustaining a 3.5 cm laceration without foreign body. Simple single-layer closure with staples performed today. Assessment: laceration of scalp, initial encounter.
Three weeks of low back pain without radiation. No red flags, no numbness or weakness, normal neurologic exam. Assessment: low back pain. Physical therapy and NSAIDs recommended.
Assessment: unilateral primary osteoarthritis of the left knee. Crepitus and pain with range of motion. Radiographs show joint space narrowing. Weight loss and physical therapy discussed.
Right shoulder pain with overhead activity. Positive Neer and Hawkins tests. Assessment: impingement syndrome of the right shoulder. Physical therapy referral placed.

Numbness and tingling in the right thumb, index, and middle fingers, worse at night. Positive Tinel and Phalen signs on the right. Assessment: carpal tunnel syndrome, right upper limb. Night splinting advised.
Heel pain worst with first steps in the morning. Tenderness at the medial calcaneal tubercle. Assessment: plantar fasciitis. Stretching program and supportive footwear advised.
Direct blow to the right knee in a fall yesterday. Ecchymosis and tenderness, no effusion, full range of motion, ligaments stable. Assessment: contusion of the right knee, initial encounter.
Right elbow pain with gripping and wrist extension. Tenderness over the lateral epicondyle. Assessment: lateral epicondylitis, right elbow. Counterforce brace and activity modification advised.
Rear-end motor vehicle collision two days ago. Posterior neck pain and stiffness, no neurologic deficit, no midline bony tenderness. Assessment: strain of neck muscle, initial encounter.
Acute onset severe pain, redness, and swelling of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint overnight. Serum uric acid elevated. Assessment: idiopathic gout, right foot. Indomethacin prescribed.

Posterior left ankle pain with running. Tenderness and thickening of the Achilles tendon, no palpable gap, Thompson test negative. Assessment: Achilles tendinitis, left leg. Eccentric loading program advised.

Progressive left shoulder stiffness over four months with global restriction of both active and passive range of motion. Assessment: adhesive capsulitis of the left shoulder. Physical therapy referral placed.

Right knee osteoarthritis with persistent pain despite conservative therapy. Assessment: unilateral primary osteoarthritis of the right knee. Arthrocentesis of the right knee performed with injection of 40 mg methylprednisolone acetate under sterile technique.

Right ear fullness and decreased hearing. Otoscopy shows impacted cerumen obscuring the right tympanic membrane. Assessment: impacted cerumen, right ear. Removal of impacted cerumen performed by instrumentation, right ear.

Patient reports intermittent palpitations for one week. Twelve-lead electrocardiogram performed in office with interpretation and report: normal sinus rhythm, no ischemic changes. Assessment: palpitations.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, stable. Spirometry performed today with graphic tracing and interpretation, showing an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.62. Assessment: COPD, unspecified.

Fluctuant abscess of the right axilla, 2 cm. Assessment: cutaneous abscess of the right axilla. Simple incision and drainage performed under local anesthesia, purulent material expressed, packing placed.
Single painful plantar wart on the left sole. Assessment: plantar wart. Destruction of the lesion performed by cryotherapy today.
Ingrown toenail of the right great toe with lateral nail fold inflammation. Assessment: ingrowing nail. Partial avulsion of the nail plate performed under digital block.
Cellulitis of the left lower limb, moderate. Assessment: cellulitis of left lower limb. Ceftriaxone 250 mg administered by intramuscular injection in the office today, followed by oral cephalexin.
Patient presents for seasonal influenza immunization. Quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine administered intramuscularly in the left deltoid. Assessment: encounter for immunization.
Patient due for tetanus booster. Tdap vaccine administered intramuscularly today. Assessment: encounter for immunization.
Dysuria and frequency for two days. Non-automated urinalysis without microscopy performed in office: positive nitrites and leukocyte esterase. Assessment: urinary tract infection, site not specified.
Sore throat with fever and tonsillar exudate. Rapid streptococcus group A antigen test performed in office, result positive. Assessment: streptococcal pharyngitis. Penicillin prescribed.
Persistent myofascial pain in the trapezius with two discrete trigger points. Assessment: myalgia. Trigger point injection performed into two muscle groups with lidocaine.
Multiple irritated skin tags in the right axilla, eight lesions removed today by snip excision. Assessment: acrochordon.
Left shoulder adhesive capsulitis with persistent pain. Assessment: adhesive capsulitis of the left shoulder. Subacromial injection of 40 mg methylprednisolone acetate performed today.

Medicare patient presents for a subsequent annual wellness visit. Health risk assessment completed, personalized prevention plan updated, cognitive assessment performed. Assessment: encounter for general adult medical examination without abnormal findings.
Average-risk patient presents to discuss colorectal cancer screening. Screening colonoscopy ordered. Assessment: encounter for screening for malignant neoplasm of the colon.
Asymptomatic patient with no breast complaints. Screening mammogram ordered. Assessment: encounter for screening mammogram for malignant neoplasm of breast.
Asymptomatic adult, no known lipid disorder. Screening fasting lipid panel ordered. Assessment: encounter for screening for lipoid disorders.
Routine visit with standardized depression screening performed using PHQ-9, scored and documented, result negative. Assessment: encounter for screening for depression.
Routine well child examination for an established 8-year-old patient, no abnormal findings. Growth and development appropriate for age. Anticipatory guidance provided.

Patient presents for routine surveillance of her established oral contraceptive pills. No side effects, blood pressure normal. Refill provided. Assessment: encounter for surveillance of contraceptive pills.
Patient smokes one pack daily and wishes to quit. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, uncomplicated. Smoking cessation counseling provided for 6 minutes, intermediate. Nicotine patch prescribed.

Asymptomatic patient with known close contact to a confirmed COVID-19 case. No symptoms today. Assessment: contact with and suspected exposure to COVID-19. Testing performed and isolation guidance given.
Obstructive sleep apnea confirmed on polysomnography with AHI of 32. Assessment: obstructive sleep apnea. Continuous positive airway pressure device ordered with humidifier.
Sprain of the left ankle sustained yesterday, initial encounter. Unable to bear weight comfortably. A pair of adjustable underarm aluminum crutches with pads, tips, and handgrips was dispensed today.
Elderly patient with unsteadiness on feet and two near-falls this month. Gait assessment performed. Assessment: unsteadiness on feet. A folding adjustable walker without wheels was dispensed today.
Chronic low back pain without radiation. Assessment: low back pain. A prefabricated off-the-shelf lumbar-sacral orthosis was dispensed in the office today for activity support.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications, requiring home glucose monitoring. A home blood glucose monitor and one box of fifty test strips were dispensed today.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unspecified, with difficulty using a metered dose inhaler. A small volume nebulizer with compressor was dispensed today.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with resting oxygen saturation of 87% on room air, qualifying for home oxygen. A stationary oxygen concentrator was ordered today.
Carpal tunnel syndrome of the right upper limb with nocturnal symptoms. A prefabricated wrist hand orthosis, off the shelf, was dispensed for night use.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy, documented on monofilament testing with loss of protective sensation. Removable molded foot inserts were dispensed today.
Patient with severe bilateral knee osteoarthritis unable to ambulate household distances. Assessment: bilateral primary osteoarthritis of knee. A standard manual wheelchair was ordered today.

New patient, 40 minutes total time. Reports two months of low mood, anhedonia, poor sleep, and difficulty concentrating. PHQ-9 score 16, consistent with moderate severity. No suicidal ideation. No prior psychiatric history. Assessment: major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate. Sertraline started.

Established patient with a history of two prior depressive episodes, now with a recurrence over six weeks. PHQ-9 score 15, moderate severity. Assessment: major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate. Dose of escitalopram increased.
Six months of excessive worry across multiple domains with restlessness and poor sleep. GAD-7 score 14. Assessment: generalized anxiety disorder. Cognitive behavioural therapy referral placed.

School-age child with longstanding inattention, distractibility, and disorganization without hyperactivity. Teacher and parent rating scales consistent. Assessment: attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive type.

Three months of difficulty initiating sleep with daytime fatigue. No sleep apnea symptoms. Assessment: insomnia, unspecified. Sleep hygiene counseling and cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia recommended.

Recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia and nausea, roughly twice monthly. Patient confirms no aura precedes the headaches. Neurologic exam normal. Assessment: migraine without aura, not intractable, no status migrainosus. Sumatriptan prescribed for abortive use.

Established patient with epilepsy, seizure free for 14 months on levetiracetam. Assessment: epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus. Continue current dose, driving restrictions reviewed.

Patient reports drinking six to eight standard drinks daily with unsuccessful attempts to cut back and morning tremor. Assessment: alcohol dependence, uncomplicated. Naltrexone discussed and counseling referral placed.
